solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bus shelters: good trap for evil spirits?

indicators.note: the word bus surrounds and protects the other pieces, as a shelter covers what is under it

parts.note: taken as the word bus itself
a gin is a snare or trap for catching animals

explanation.surface: A spooky suggestion that bus shelters could serve as traps for ghosts and demons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelters' signals a container. The definition is an old dialect word for hobgoblins, related to bug and bugbear; 'trap' is the gin of a gin trap, not a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic dialect word for bogeys or hobgoblins, kin to bugbear, so it names malign supernatural beings.

clue.text: Perhaps widowed female wearing traditional headgear

indicators.note: the letter is worn by the hat, so it sits inside it

parts.note: the beret is the traditional cap of the Basques

explanation.surface: A widow in mourning dons a traditional hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Being widowed is one instance of being deprived of a loved one, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Lords changing political allegiance gradually

indicators.note: moving from right to left politically swaps an R for an L

parts.note: the gentry are the landed upper class, lords and nobles

explanation.surface: Members of the House of Lords slowly crossing the floor to another party.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) becomes L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: doing something softly and by degrees means doing it slowly and carefully.

clue.text: Cursed outburst of acid temper

indicators.note: an outburst bursts the words apart, so their letters are scattered and re-formed

explanation.surface: Someone swore during a fit of sharp, bitter anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to imprecate is to invoke evil upon, so the past tense means swore at or damned.

clue.text: Burn spruce

definitions.meaning: to sting or feel a sharp burning pain
neat and stylish in appearance, well turned out

explanation.surface: A fire threatens a coniferous tree.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to sting painfully; as an adjective it means neat, trim and well dressed.

clue.text: Bendy bus under control? And the other half?

indicators.note: something under control is in hand, so the jumbled letters sit within the word for control

parts.note: to have something in hand is to have it under control

indicators.note: a bendy thing is bent out of shape, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzled commuter asks whether an articulated bus is under control, then wonders about its other half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bendy' is the anagram signal, and 'under control' is read as 'in hand', so the jumbled bus sits inside the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Other half is an informal idiom for one's spouse or partner, here a married man.

clue.text: Tubes destined for Green Park?

parts.note: Green Park is a London Underground station on the Tube, but here green park means a lawn kept green by watering through tubes

explanation.surface: London Underground trains heading for Green Park station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tubes' and 'Green Park' suggest the London Underground, Green Park being a central Tube station; the real tubes are garden ones for watering.
explanation.definitionFit: Flexible tubes used for watering are what keep a park's grass lush and green.

clue.text: It's foul being this poorly without the end in sight

indicators.note: the phrase loses its end, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: so ill means this poorly, ill meaning poorly and so meaning this much

explanation.surface: A sick person complains that being this unwell with no end in sight is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without the end' drops the final L of SO ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs: to soil something is to dirty or befoul it.

clue.text: A 'flat' young ale brewed in the old-fashioned way

indicators.note: brewing works ingredients into something new, so these letters are rearranged
a flat beer has no head, so the word young loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A traditionally brewed ale, served young and without fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' is the beheading signal, since a flat beer has no head, and 'brewed' the anagram signal. The quotation marks warn that 'flat' is not describing the ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Analogue technology predates digital, so it is the older, traditional way of doing things.

clue.text: Tend a toe that's injured and set off

indicators.note: an injured toe is damaged and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nurse a hurt toe and then head off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to explode a bomb or charge is to set it off.

clue.text: Devise approach

definitions.meaning: to make or put together quickly
the lead-up or preparatory period before an event

explanation.surface: Two bare words: invent something, and the way you come towards it.
explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb it means to make hastily; as a noun it is the lead-in period or approach to something.

clue.text: Attacker like skipper a nutcase

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of in the manner of
to skipper a boat is to sail it, taking the verb sense
read as the case of nut, its outside letters, the first and last

explanation.surface: An assailant described as being like a ship's captain who is also a madman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nutcase' splits into 'nut' plus 'case', the case being the shell or outside letters, NT. 'skipper' is read as a verb, to sail.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is one who assails, that is someone who launches a physical or verbal assault.

clue.text: Riddle plus clues which are drawn on out of habit?

definitions.text: which are drawn on out of habit?

parts.note: a riddle is a coarse sieve, and to riddle is to sift or strain
tips are hints or clues that help someone

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter bundles a riddle with some clues that solvers pore over habitually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle but is the sieve sense. The definition refers to cigarettes: smokers draw on them out of habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Cigarette ends fitted with a filter are what a habitual smoker inhales through, drawing on them out of addiction.

clue.text: Idiot abandons woodwind, which could be a blessing

indicators.note: the fool leaves the instrument behind, so his letters are taken out of it

parts.note: a bassoon is a large woodwind instrument
an ass is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: A clumsy musician giving up a wind instrument might be a mercy for the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a boon is a welcome benefit or blessing that improves someone's lot.

clue.text: Slimmers' cheese creates conflict with neighbours

parts.note: lo-cal, short for low-calorie, describes food for slimmers
Derby is an English cheese

explanation.surface: A low-fat cheese sparks a quarrel with the people next door.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby is a hard English cow's-milk cheese. A local derby is a match between two nearby rival teams.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting match between neighbouring rival teams, such as two clubs from one city, is a contest between neighbours.

clue.text: Lavish specialist channel is rubbish

parts.note: to lavish money is to squander or waste it
a pro is a professional, someone expert in a field
a duct is a tube or channel carrying fluid or air

explanation.surface: A TV critic sneers that a lavish niche channel broadcasts nothing but garbage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: discarded material left over by a process is junk, refuse or trash.

clue.text: Article in Times on a patchwork of lies causing torment

indicators.note: the article goes inside the two abbreviations for time

parts.note: T is an abbreviation for time, so two of them make times
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: a patchwork is pieced together from scraps, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A newspaper article built from scraps of falsehood causes anguish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but gives T twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to tantalise is to tease or torment with something just out of reach, as Tantalus was.

clue.text: Top group second to Yes in Germany fear musical fusion

indicators.note: the band comes second, right after the German word, placing it later in the run

parts.note: ja is German for yes
ZZ Top is a rock band, so the group with Top gives ZZ
a funk is a state of fear or panic, as in a blue funk

explanation.surface: A chart-topping band ranks just behind the band Yes in Germany, out of fear.
explanation.walkthrough: ZZ Top is an American rock band; 'Yes' looks like the prog-rock band but is just the German word.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre blending jazz improvisation with funk rhythms, so it is a hybrid style of music.

clue.text: Drug dealer quick to limit damage

indicators.note: the word for quick hems in and limits the word for damage

parts.note: pacy means fast or quick
harm is damage or injury

explanation.surface: A narcotics pusher eager to minimise harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug dealer' sounds criminal but means a chemist's shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist's shop legitimately sells medicines, so it literally deals in drugs.

clue.text: Dash newsy idea off wanting one to make fast start

indicators.note: an off idea has gone bad or awry, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An editor tells a writer to scrap a newsy idea that lacks one quick start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting one' says the letters of DASH NEWSY IDEA lose an I before 'off' rearranges them. The day starts Lent, a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: This Wednesday begins the Christian fasting season of Lent, so it is literally the beginning of a fast.

clue.text: Fool departs for good in flood

indicators.note: one letter stands in for another, taking its place

parts.note: a deluge is a great flood
D is short for departs in timetables

explanation.surface: Leaving for good during a flood would be a foolish trick.
explanation.walkthrough: D (departs) replaces G (good) in DELUGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs: to delude someone is to deceive or fool them.

clue.text: Line on weather map as a result of which key is to check air for pollution

indicators.note: the jumbled air holds back or contains the other letters, checking them in place
polluted air is fouled up, so its letters are disordered

parts.note: so means therefore, as a result of which
B is a musical key

explanation.surface: A meteorologist explains a line on the forecast chart as a result of testing air quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for pollution' is the anagram signal and 'to check' the container: the scrambled air holds the other pieces in check.
explanation.definitionFit: A line joining points of equal atmospheric pressure, drawn on weather charts.

clue.text: Downsize roomy accommodation for nothing

indicators.note: the two words house the solution, giving it accommodation across their join

explanation.surface: Moving from a spacious home to a smaller one for no money at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: the numeral nought, nil or naught names an absence of quantity.

clue.text: Like the idea of force devoid of uniform or distinctive costume

parts.note: to fancy something is to like the idea of it

indicators.note: being without the letter means it is removed from the word for force

parts.note: duress is compulsion or force
Uniform is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for U

explanation.surface: Someone toys with dressing up but is told it is either a uniform or an unusual outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devoid of uniform' strips U from DURESS to give DRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Costume worn to a party to look like a character or theme is an eye-catching outfit of this kind.

clue.text: Penned most of page in post-7 medium

indicators.note: the shortened word sits within the recording medium

parts.note: the medium coming after analogue (the solution to 7) is the digital compact disc, CD

indicators.note: most of the word means one letter is dropped, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: Most of a page written for a modern format.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 7 down: the compact disc is the medium that followed analogue recordings.
explanation.definitionFit: Penned means shut in a pen, synonymous with confined behind bars.

clue.text: 16 player maybe starts to mess up string orchestration

indicators.note: the starts of the next four words are their initial letters

explanation.surface: A jazz-funk musician begins to botch the string arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 refers to 16 down, a style of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A muso is a slang term for a musician, and a jazz-funk player is one example.

clue.text: How we found a Victorian equerry's joke?

definitions.text: How we found a Victorian equerry's joke?

parts.words: How we found a Victorian equerry's joke?
parts.note: Queen Victoria is said to have rebuked a courtier's risqué story with the words 'We are not amused', using the royal we

explanation.surface: A courtier's story told to Queen Victoria, and her famously frosty reaction to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we' is the royal we of Queen Victoria's legendary put-down of a joke told at court.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen's reported verdict on the courtier's story was that it was not funny, which is what the adjective says.

clue.text: Line from Pooh composition bridging rhythm and blues

indicators.note: the song spans the gap between the two letters, sitting between them

parts.note: R and B is the usual short form, its initials R and B
Winnie-the-Pooh composes little songs he calls hums

explanation.surface: A lyric from one of Winnie-the-Pooh's songs that blends rhythm and blues.
explanation.walkthrough: Winnie-the-Pooh, A. A. Milne's bear, makes up songs he calls hums.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigational term for a course or line crossing every meridian at the same angle, a loxodrome.

clue.text: Island house the French will make a tempting prospect for some?

parts.note: a key is a low island or reef, as in the Florida Keys
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French-owned island home sounds like an alluring prospect for buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to snoopers, for whom a view through a door's small opening is tempting.
explanation.definitionFit: Peeping through a door's lock opening tempts the nosy, offering a sneaky view of a room.

clue.text: Offbeat way to sport favourite regular outfit

indicators.note: to sport something is to wear it, so the word for favourite wears the jumbled letters inside it

parts.note: a dear is a favourite or beloved person

indicators.note: offbeat means unconventional or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unconventional way to wear your favourite everyday clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offbeat' is the anagram signal; 'to sport' means to wear, so the favourite wears the jumbled way inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes for ordinary daily use, as opposed to evening or special-occasion wear, form a normal outfit.
